title: U.S. House · Vermont At-Large
area: The entire state of Vermont, which has a single at-large U.S. House district.

context.text: Incumbent Becca Balint (D) advanced from the Democratic primary on August 11, 2026 with 98.3% of the vote. Gerald Malloy defeated Mark Coester in the Republican primary with 76.6% of the vote.

candidates.name: Becca Balint
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11 Democratic primary with 98.3% of the vote

summary.text: Becca Balint is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Vermont's at-large district, seeking re-election in 2026. She previously served in the Vermont State Senate, including as President Pro Tempore.

background.text: Born at a U.S. Army hospital in Heidelberg, Germany; lives in Brattleboro, Vermont.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Smith College, a master's degree in education from Harvard University (1995), and a master's degree in history from the University of Massachusetts at Amherst (2001).
Worked as a teacher in public and private schools before entering politics.
Served in the Vermont State Senate, including as Senate President Pro Tempore, before her election to Congress in 2022.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on the Judiciary (Subcommittee on the Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust; Subcommittee on the Constitution and Limited Government) and the House Committee on the Budget for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Gerald Malloy
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11 Republican primary with 76.6% of the vote

summary.text: Gerald Malloy is a retired U.S. Army officer and business executive running as the Republican nominee for Vermont's at-large House seat.

background.text: Born in Boston, Massachusetts; lives in Perkinsville, Vermont.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1980 to 2006, entering West Point at age 18.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point (1984), a graduate degree from Temple University (1996), and a graduate certificate from Georgetown University (2021).
Career experience includes working as a business executive after his military service.

priorities.text: "I will: bring high-paying jobs back to Vermont, Cut unnecessary federal regulations that hold back small businesses, Support local industries—dairy, agriculture, and manufacturing... Push for fiscal discipline in Washington to reduce inflation."

"Washington's overspending is driving inflation and making life more expensive. I will: Oppose tax increases on Vermont families, Work toward balanced budgets, Protect and strengthen Social Security and Medicare—without cutting benefits."
"I will always stand for the Constitution and the rights of every Vermonter... Uphold the 10th Amendment and states' rights... Oppose federal overreach on issues better decided locally."

positions.summary: Describes himself as pro-life and says decisions on abortion should be left to the states rather than the Supreme Court.
positions.quote: Pro life. Per the 10th Amendment I support taking this decision out of the Supreme Court and giving it to States and People.

positions.summary: Says he supports the Second Amendment and is a gun owner.
positions.quote: Fully support all Amendments, including 2d Amendment Right to Bear Arms. I am a gun owner, my wife is an NRA member.

positions.summary: Says he will enforce and change immigration laws and secure the southern border.
positions.quote: I will seek to enforce immigration laws, and change immigration laws as necessary. I will secure our southern border to address the crime, Opioid/Fentanyl, and illegal immigration crisis.

positions.summary: Criticizes state climate legislation such as Vermont's Global Warming Solutions Act and says he wants to restore U.S. oil and gas independence.
positions.quote: I am passionate about restoring US oil and gas independence.

summary.text: Adam Ortiz is running as an independent candidate for Vermont's at-large U.S. House seat. He is a U.S. Army National Guard veteran (2006-2012) and completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, in which he described environmental protection and infrastructure investment as priorities.
